Execute SQL file with parameter interpolation

Source: R/load_sql_query.R
execute_sql_file.Rd

Convenience wrapper that loads and executes a SQL file in one step.

Usage

execute_sql_file(
  sql,
  conn,
  execute = TRUE,
  save_as_parquet = FALSE,
  parquet_path = NULL,
  partition_by = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

sql

A sql query string typically loaded via load_sql_query()

conn

DBI connection object

execute

logical; if TRUE (default), execute the query. If FALSE, return the interpolated SQL string.

save_as_parquet

logical; if TRUE, saves the result of a SELECT query to Parquet. For DuckDB connections, the query result is streamed directly to disk via DuckDB's COPY ... TO ... (FORMAT PARQUET), without materialising it as an R data.frame first. Other DBI backends fall back to DBI::dbGetQuery() + arrow::write_dataset().

parquet_path

character; file path to save the Parquet file if save as_parquet is TRUE. Required if save_as_parquet is TRUE.

partition_by

vector of column names to partition the Parquet file

...

additional arguments passed to DBI::dbExecute or DBI::dbGetQuery

Value

If execute = TRUE and save_as_parquet = TRUE on a DuckDB connection, returns invisible(parquet_path). Otherwise, if execute = TRUE, returns the result from DBI. If FALSE, returns the SQL string.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Execute SQL file with parameters
execute_sql_file(
  sql,
  conn = my_conn,
  file_path = "queries/create_table.sql",
  params = list(
    schema = "staging",
    table = "temp_data"
  )
)
} # }
